items.title: No skill measure in the programme
items.whyItMatters: Without a baseline and a blinded score, no change can be seen.
items.opportunity: Film one index operation per resident at the start and end of the year and rate edited videos blind.

items.title: Residents who choose coaching differ
items.whyItMatters: Self-selection inflated the only comparative estimate (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Record baseline score and training year and adjust for both; report the comparison as an association.

items.title: Fear that videos will be used for assessment
items.whyItMatters: Junior and female residents were more worried (claim c3), which could bias who takes part.
items.opportunity: Keep study videos out of assessment and delete them after rating.

items.title: Patient outcomes not linked to coaching
items.whyItMatters: Skill scores are a surrogate; complications are too rare to study in 14 residents.
items.opportunity: State the surrogate honestly; do not claim patient benefit.

errorsFound: The request assumes coaching helps because residents like it; liking is not evidence of skill gain.
reevaluation: A prospective comparison with blinded rating and adjustment for baseline skill is the honest minimum; the estimate will be imprecise with 14 residents.
summary: Four gaps: no skill measure, self-selection, fear of assessment use, and surrogate outcomes.
